stories.headline: Houthis threaten Saudi ports and Riyadh after strikes on Yemen
body: Yemen's Houthis threatened Saudi ports, a power station and the capital, Riyadh.
It came after the Saudi-led coalition said it hit the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah, and Sanaa was also struck.
The Houthis told people to leave Saudi Red Sea ports.
stories.vc: Threats to Red Sea ports raise shipping and insurance costs.

stories.headline: Spain's far-right Vox could be kingmaker in snap election
body: Spain votes in a snap election on November 29.
Polls put far-right Vox third, but the leading Popular Party may need its support to govern.
Vox is campaigning on mass deportations and 'national priority' for benefits.
stories.joke: Kingmaker: the job nobody applies for, but everyone wants.
stories.vc: A hard-right coalition could shift Spain's policy on migration and EU funds.

stories.headline: Sudan's war shuts schools for disabled children
body: Sudan's war has closed the special schools and rehab centres that disabled children rely on.
Four-year-old Muzan, who has a hearing impairment, can't get the help she needs to start school.
The war began in April 2023 and shows no sign of ending.
stories.vc: Aid donors are under pressure to fund education in war zones.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 898 points as banks lead a comeback
body: The Sensex rose 897.96 points to 83,919.71 on Friday; the Nifty closed at 25,800.60.
Markets opened lower after a global sell-off, then banks, IT and healthcare led a rebound.
Apollo Hospitals, Axis Bank and Maruti were among the gainers.
stories.joke: Down in the morning, up by lunch. Classic Friday.
stories.vc: India is holding up while US tech stocks slide.

stories.headline: Urban Company raises ₹2,500 crore as bids top ₹15,000 crore
body: Urban Company raised ₹2,500 crore from big investors, with bids worth over ₹15,000 crore.
More than 60 investors bid; mutual funds took over half.
₹600 crore will go to its 10-minute house-help service, InstaHelp.
stories.joke: Demand for house help, and for its shares.
stories.vc: Strong demand shows investors still back loss-making growth bets.

stories.headline: Supreme Court clears the way for bike taxis in Karnataka
body: The Supreme Court dismissed Karnataka's appeal against a High Court order allowing bike taxis.
That lets Ola, Uber and Rapido run two-wheeler taxis in the state.
The bench said regulation beats a blanket ban, and GPS bike taxis are safer for women.
stories.joke: Bengaluru traffic, now with more weaving.
stories.vc: A green light for a cheap, fast-growing ride market.

stories.headline: Anthropic slides a day after its record IPO as AI stocks fall
body: Anthropic shares fell about 9.5% on Friday morning to near $88, still above the $83 IPO price.
It briefly topped $2 trillion in value after listing.
The slide came amid a wider AI stock sell-off. (No new FT/Unhedged piece, so this is Al Jazeera's report.)
stories.joke: Day one: party. Day two: hangover.
stories.vc: A weak follow-through could cool other AI IPO plans.

stories.headline: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68 billion
body: Bending Spoons is buying email firm Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion.
Intuit paid about $12 billion for it in 2021.
Intuit's shares have more than halved in a year. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's deal.)
stories.vc: AI fears are pushing down prices for older software firms.

stories.headline: Government space fund backs SatSure in ₹200 crore round
body: The Centre's Antariksh Venture Capital Fund put ₹60 crore into SatSure, the first part of a ₹200 crore round.
It values the satellite-data startup at ₹870 crore.
It's the fund's second bet after Dhruva Space. (TechCrunch Venture had no fresh India deal, so this is Inc42's.)
stories.joke: Eyes in the sky, money on the ground.
stories.vc: State-backed funds are helping India's space startups raise money.

stories.statLabel: Huang's chances of returning, per Sharp Tech
stories.headline: Stratechery: Jensen Huang is not coming back
body: On Sharp Tech, Ben Thompson and Andrew Sharp argue Jensen Huang won't return to Nvidia.
They also discuss AI shopping agents.
And Thompson reviews the iPhone Duo.
stories.vc: A settled leadership question would help Nvidia move on.

stories.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over Huang's China ties
body: California's attorney general has served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena.
He is probing whether chips or secrets reached China, and whether investors were misled.
Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy prompted the probe. (No checkable Economist piece, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Stacking probes keep legal risk hanging over Nvidia shares.

stories.headline: C-sections hit 69% of births in insured private-hospital claims
body: C-sections made up 69% of over 1.6 lakh delivery-related insurance claims studied, a record.
The data from insurer Plum covers corporate and white-collar workers.
Medical reasons include breech babies, placenta problems and high blood pressure.
stories.vc: Avoidable surgery raises costs for families, employers and insurers.

stories.statLabel: findings of misconduct to be disclosed
stories.headline: House Ethics changes how it handles sexual misconduct claims
body: The US House Ethics Committee changed its rules for sexual misconduct cases.
It will publicly disclose when members are found to have committed harassment, keeping victims anonymous.
It also cut delays in investigations.
stories.vc: Clearer rules can reduce legal and reputational risk for Congress.

stories.headline: Hyderabad government hospital's IVF centre helps a mother have triplets
body: After nine years and failed private treatment, a 32-year-old mother had triplet boys after care at Gandhi Hospital's IVF centre.
The premature babies spent over a month in its newborn ICU.
Mother and babies have gone home.
stories.joke: Three for the price of one government hospital visit.
stories.vc: Public fertility care makes costly treatment reachable for more families.

stories.headline: Andhra plans robotic surgery in government teaching hospitals
body: Andhra Pradesh plans robotic surgeries in government teaching hospitals, starting with a ₹45 crore centre in Vijayawada.
KGH Visakhapatnam and GGH Kurnool would follow.
IVF and bone marrow transplant centres are also proposed.
stories.joke: Robots in the operating theatre, on the state's tab.
stories.vc: High-end surgery in public hospitals cuts costs for poorer patients.

stories.headline: All government medical colleges told to join PM-RAHAT crash-care scheme
body: The National Medical Commission asked all government medical colleges and their hospitals to join PM-RAHAT.
The scheme offers cashless emergency treatment to road accident victims.
The health ministry asked for wider sign-up.
stories.vc: More hospitals in the scheme means faster care in the 'golden hour'.

stories.headline: Chennai's SRM Prime Hospital adds advanced laser for prostate and stones
body: SRM Prime Hospital in Ramapuram has added a Holmium laser system for enlarged prostates and urinary stones.
It allows minimally invasive procedures with less bleeding.
Patients may recover faster and stay in hospital less.
stories.joke: Lasers: not just for sci-fi anymore.
stories.vc: New tech helps private hospitals compete for surgical patients.

stories.headline: SEBI shows off its AI market watchdogs to Asia's regulators
body: SEBI hosted Asia-Pacific securities regulators in Mumbai and showed its AI and SupTech tools.
SupTech means software regulators use to spot rule-breaking.
Talks also covered faster settlement and tokenisation.
stories.joke: The referee now has a robot whistle.
stories.vc: Smarter surveillance makes manipulation harder for fast traders.

stories.headline: Tokenised assets can move instantly, but liquidity lags
body: Panellists from Tradeweb, Goldman Sachs and Fnality say tokenised assets still lack liquid markets.
Moving an asset instantly isn't the same as having buyers and sellers.
Secondary trading, repo and digital cash must grow together.
stories.vc: Thin tokenised markets limit room for market makers for now.

stories.headline: Explainer: What does it mean to 'tokenise' a share?
body: Imagine your school gives you a digital sticker that stands for one cricket card in the class cupboard.
You can swap the sticker with a friend in a second, and the card in the cupboard now belongs to them.
Grown-ups call this tokenisation: turning things like shares or bonds into digital tokens.
This week SEBI discussed tokenisation with other countries' market regulators in Mumbai.
It could make trading faster and open all day, but only if enough people want to buy and sell.
stories.vc: Faster markets, if there are enough traders.

stories.headline: F1 agrees to bring back V8 engines from 2030
body: The FIA says it has unanimous agreement with F1 and engine makers to return to V8 engines.
F1 wants cheaper, simpler engines after deciding today's units are too complex and heavy.
Cadillac has already dropped plans to build its own V6 hybrid.
stories.vc: Cheaper engines could lure new manufacturers and cut team costs.
